# viettelcloud_dbc_cluster (Resource)

Manage a Viettel Cloud DB cluster. Supports the cassandra, memcached, mongodb, opensearch, starrocks and timescaledb engines. Only description and keep_backup change in place. Changing any other argument replaces the cluster and deletes its data, so protect a production cluster with `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "db_root_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

resource "viettelcloud_vpc" "example" {
  name   = "db-example-vpc"
  cidr   = "10.0.0.0/16"
  region = { name = "vn-central-1" }
}

resource "viettelcloud_subnet" "example" {
  name = "db-example-subnet"
  cidr = "10.0.1.0/24"
  vpc  = { id = viettelcloud_vpc.example.id }
}

# A MongoDB replica set. The node pool is named mongo for mongo_rs and shard
# for mongo_sharding, and a sharded cluster also sets partition_count to the
# number of shards.
resource "viettelcloud_dbc_cluster" "mongodb" {
  name           = "example-mongodb"
  description    = "Orders database"
  engine         = "mongodb"
  engine_version = { version = "7.0" }
  region         = { name = "vn-central-1" }
  subnet         = { id = viettelcloud_subnet.example.id }
  topology       = "mongo_rs"

  # root_password is write-only: Terraform sends it when it creates the cluster
  # and never stores it. Changing it later has no effect.
  root_password = var.db_root_password

  node_pools = [{
    name            = "mongo"
    replicas        = 3
    resource_config = { name = "2c4g" }
    storage_class   = { name = "ssd" }
    disk_size       = 100
  }]

  auto_backup_config = {
    enable_auto_backup = true
    backup_interval    = "weekly"
    day_of_week        = "sunday"
    start_hour         = 2
    max_auto_backup    = 7
  }

  # Only description and keep_backup change in place. Changing anything else,
  # such as the node pools or the backup schedule, replaces the cluster and
  # deletes its data, so keep this on a cluster that holds real data.
  lifecycle {
    prevent_destroy = true
  }
}

# An OpenSearch cluster. It takes no topology, and its node pools are named by
# you. The cluster needs at least one data node and three cluster manager
# nodes in total.
resource "viettelcloud_dbc_cluster" "opensearch" {
  name           = "example-opensearch"
  engine         = "opensearch"
  engine_version = { version = "2.11" }
  region         = { name = "vn-central-1" }
  subnet         = { id = viettelcloud_subnet.example.id }

  root_password = var.db_root_password

  node_pools = [
    {
      name            = "manager"
      replicas        = 3
      resource_config = { name = "2c4g" }
      storage_class   = { name = "ssd" }
      disk_size       = 50
      engine_roles    = ["cluster_manager"]
    },
    {
      name            = "data"
      replicas        = 2
      resource_config = { name = "4c8g" }
      storage_class   = { name = "ssd" }
      disk_size       = 200
      engine_roles    = ["data", "ingest"]
      pool_config     = { attribute = "hot" }
    },
  ]

  plugins = [{ name = "analysis-icu" }]
}

# A Cassandra cluster. It takes no topology and one node pool named cassandra.
# The backend always disables SSL for Cassandra.
resource "viettelcloud_dbc_cluster" "cassandra" {
  name           = "example-cassandra"
  engine         = "cassandra"
  engine_version = { version = "4.1" }
  region         = { name = "vn-central-1" }
  subnet         = { id = viettelcloud_subnet.example.id }

  root_password = var.db_root_password

  node_pools = [{
    name            = "cassandra"
    replicas        = 3
    resource_config = { name = "4c8g" }
    storage_class   = { name = "ssd" }
    disk_size       = 100
  }]
}

# A Memcached cluster. Its nodes keep data in memory, so its node pools take
# no storage_class or disk_size, and it has no backups. The mcrouter mode also
# needs a node pool named mcrouter.
resource "viettelcloud_dbc_cluster" "memcached" {
  name           = "example-memcached"
  engine         = "memcached"
  engine_version = { version = "1.6" }
  region         = { name = "vn-central-1" }
  subnet         = { id = viettelcloud_subnet.example.id }

  root_password = var.db_root_password

  engine_config = {
    mode         = "direct"
    auth_enabled = true
  }

  node_pools = [{
    name            = "memcached"
    replicas        = 2
    resource_config = { name = "2c4g" }
  }]
}

# A StarRocks cluster. It takes two node pools named fe and be. The fe pool
# has 1 or 3 replicas, and the be pool an odd number up to 9. The backend
# always disables SSL for StarRocks, and the engine has no backups.
resource "viettelcloud_dbc_cluster" "starrocks" {
  name           = "example-starrocks"
  engine         = "starrocks"
  engine_version = { version = "3.2" }
  region         = { name = "vn-central-1" }
  subnet         = { id = viettelcloud_subnet.example.id }

  root_password = var.db_root_password

  node_pools = [
    {
      name            = "fe"
      replicas        = 1
      resource_config = { name = "2c4g" }
      storage_class   = { name = "ssd" }
      disk_size       = 50
    },
    {
      name            = "be"
      replicas        = 3
      resource_config = { name = "4c8g" }
      storage_class   = { name = "ssd" }
      disk_size       = 200
    },
  ]
}

# A TimescaleDB cluster. It takes one node pool with a name of your choice.
# It keeps backups for retention_days, and point-in-time recovery comes on
# together with the backup schedule.
resource "viettelcloud_dbc_cluster" "timescaledb" {
  name           = "example-timescaledb"
  engine         = "timescaledb"
  engine_version = { version = "17" }
  region         = { name = "vn-central-1" }
  subnet         = { id = viettelcloud_subnet.example.id }

  root_password = var.db_root_password

  node_pools = [{
    name            = "db"
    replicas        = 1
    resource_config = { name = "2c4g" }
    storage_class   = { name = "ssd" }
    disk_size       = 100
  }]

  enable_pitr_backup = true
  auto_backup_config = {
    enable_auto_backup = true
    backup_interval    = "daily"
    start_hour         = 1
    retention_days     = 14
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `engine` (String) Database engine: cassandra, memcached, mongodb, opensearch, starrocks or timescaledb.
- `engine_version` (Attributes) Active engine version of the selected engine. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--engine_version))
- `name` (String) Name of the DB cluster. It is unique per project and engine.
- `node_pools` (Attributes List) Node pools of the cluster. mongodb takes exactly one pool, named mongo for mongo_rs and shard for mongo_sharding. cassandra takes one pool named cassandra. memcached takes a pool named memcached, plus a pool named mcrouter when engine_config.mode is mcrouter. starrocks takes two pools named fe and be. opensearch takes one or more pools, and timescaledb exactly one pool, with names of your choice. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--node_pools))
- `region` (Attributes) Project region where the cluster is created. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--region))
- `root_password` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Password of the administrator account. It is used only when the cluster is created. Terraform never stores it in the plan or the state, so changing it later has no effect and does not change the password of the cluster.
- `subnet` (Attributes) Private subnet that the cluster connects to. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--subnet))

### Optional

- `allowed_cidrs` (Set of String) IPv4 CIDR blocks that may connect to the cluster, such as 10.0.0.5/32. A bare address without a prefix length is rejected.
- `auto_backup_config` (Attributes) Automatic backup schedule. When omitted, the cluster has no schedule. The memcached and starrocks engines have no backups and reject it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--auto_backup_config))
- `description` (String) Description of the DB cluster. Set it to an empty string to clear it.
- `enable_auto_increase_volume_size` (Boolean) Whether the backend grows node volumes automatically. The backend defaults to false.
- `enable_pitr_backup` (Boolean) Whether point-in-time recovery is enabled. mongodb and timescaledb only, and it needs auto_backup_config with enable_auto_backup set to true. The backend defaults to false.
- `enable_public_access` (Boolean) Whether the cluster is reachable from the internet. The backend defaults to false.
- `enable_ssl` (Boolean) Whether connections use SSL. The backend defaults to false, always enables it for the opensearch engine and the mongo_sharding topology, and always disables it for the cassandra and starrocks engines.
- `engine_config` (Attributes) Engine settings. memcached only; the other engines have no settings and reject it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--engine_config))
- `keep_backup` (Boolean) Whether the backups of the cluster are kept when the cluster is deleted. The backend defaults to true. The opensearch engine always deletes its backups, so it accepts false only.
- `maintenance_config` (Attributes) Weekly maintenance window. The backend defaults to Sunday at hour 0. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--maintenance_config))
- `metadata` (Map of String) Free-form string metadata of the cluster.
- `plugins` (Attributes Set) Plugins to install. opensearch only. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--plugins))
- `topology` (String) Topology of the cluster. Required for mongodb: mongo_rs or mongo_sharding. Must be omitted for the other engines, which have a single topology.
- `zone` (Attributes) Project zone of the cluster. Omit it for a multi-zone cluster. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--zone))

### Read-Only

- `admin_username` (String) Username of the administrator account.
- `created_at` (String) Timestamp when the cluster was created (RFC3339).
- `enable_auto_backup` (Boolean) Whether automatic backup is enabled. Set it with auto_backup_config.
- `endpoint` (Map of String) Connection endpoint that the backend reports. A value that is not a string is encoded as JSON.
- `error_message` (String) Error message of the last failed operation.
- `id` (String) DB cluster ID (UUID).
- `operational_status` (String) Operation that the backend is running on the cluster, or noop.
- `status` (String) Status of the cluster, such as active.
- `updated_at` (String) Timestamp when the cluster was last updated (RFC3339).

<a id="nestedatt--engine_version"></a>
### Nested Schema for `engine_version`

Required:

- `version` (String) Exact engine version, e.g. 7.0.


<a id="nestedatt--node_pools"></a>
### Nested Schema for `node_pools`

Required:

- `name` (String) Name of the node pool.
- `replicas` (Number) Number of replicas in the pool.
- `resource_config` (Attributes) CPU and memory package of each node. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--node_pools--resource_config))

Optional:

- `disk_size` (Number) Requested volume size of each node in GB. Required for every engine except memcached, whose nodes have no volume and reject it. The backend can grow a volume past this size when enable_auto_increase_volume_size is true, so Terraform keeps your value. Read actual_disk_size for the size in use. A size above the volume in use replaces the cluster. A size that is not larger is recorded without changing the volume, because a volume never shrinks.
- `engine_roles` (Set of String) Engine roles of the pool. opensearch only: data, cluster_manager, ingest or coordinating.
- `partition_count` (Number) Number of partitions. For the mongo_sharding topology this is the number of shards and is required. The backend defaults it to 1 elsewhere.
- `pool_config` (Attributes) Engine-specific settings of the pool. opensearch only. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--node_pools--pool_config))
- `storage_class` (Attributes) Storage class of the node volumes. Required for every engine except memcached, whose nodes have no volume and reject it. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--node_pools--storage_class))

Read-Only:

- `actual_disk_size` (Number) Volume size of each node in GB as the backend reports it.
- `id` (String) Node pool ID (UUID).
- `node_count` (Number) Number of nodes in the pool: replicas multiplied by partition_count.
- `role` (String) Role that the backend gives the pool in the topology.
- `used_disk_size` (Number) Used volume space of each node as the backend reports it.

<a id="nestedatt--auto_backup_config"></a>
### Nested Schema for `auto_backup_config`

Required:

- `backup_interval` (String) Backup interval: daily or weekly.
- `enable_auto_backup` (Boolean) Whether automatic backup is enabled.
- `start_hour` (Number) Hour of day that the backup starts, 0 to 23, in backend time.

Optional:

- `day_of_week` (String) Lowercase day name, such as monday. Required for weekly backups and rejected for daily backups.
- `max_auto_backup` (Number) Number of automatic backups to keep. Required for every engine with backups except timescaledb, which rejects it.
- `retention_days` (Number) Number of days to keep automatic backups. Required for timescaledb and rejected for the other engines.


<a id="nestedatt--engine_config"></a>
### Nested Schema for `engine_config`

Optional:

- `auth_enabled` (Boolean) Whether clients must authenticate. The backend defaults to false, and the mcrouter mode does not support it.
- `mcrouter_routing_type` (String) Routing of the mcrouter mode: sharded or replicated. Required for the mcrouter mode and rejected otherwise.
- `mode` (String) Memcached mode: direct or mcrouter. The backend defaults to direct.


<a id="nestedatt--maintenance_config"></a>
### Nested Schema for `maintenance_config`

Optional:

- `day_of_week` (String) Lowercase day name, such as sunday.
- `start_hour` (Number) Hour of day that maintenance starts, 0 to 23, in backend time.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a DB cluster by ID. The configuration must declare every required
# argument, including root_password, which is write-only and so is never read
# back from the cluster.
terraform import viettelcloud_dbc_cluster.mongodb 6f1a2c3d-4e5b-6789-abcd-ef0123456789

# An OpenSearch cluster reports its node pools sorted by name. List the pools
# in that order in the configuration to import it without a state-only update.
# Import also records the volume size in use for each pool. A disk_size that is
# not larger than that size never replaces the cluster.
```
